Reserve inner1 for an uninterrupted GND reference. Prefer top USB paths over inner1; any bottom/inner2 fallback requires reference-plane review and nearby ground stitching for return paths.

Route paired branches adjacently, with equal transition counts where possible. Review total connector-to-MCU DP and DM lengths across PORT, SWITCH and MCU nets; maxLength values are detour caps, not verified skew limits.

The fixed interleaved connector pads and reversed north-facing MCU-side resistor terminals require detours; clearance-aware realization must not replace these endpoint trees with straight segments through intervening pads.

All eleven owned nets have explicit spanning trees. ESD pin1/pin6 and pin3/pin4 are connected through PCB copper so protection can remain in the routed path. Physical ESD/package behavior still requires component validation.
Routing intent is not fabrication qualified: clearance, completed copper, thermal rise, stackup, via current capacity and switching behavior need validation.
Reserve inner1 for continuous GND. Prefer top for bridge/driver/bootstrap; bottom is available for quiet Kelvin branches and remote DC feeds.
Nominal 1–2 mm power corridors require short pad necks. U_INPUT pin5/pin6 polygon lands are 0.30 mm wide; use 0.20 mm escape only locally. Never silently accept long 0.20 mm power runs.

Kelvin pairs originate at R20 lands and carry no power. Keep R25/R26 and R41/R42 branches away from TEC_SW, gates, inductor and high-current corridors; same-net geometric merging must not collapse these into power trunks.

Q20/Q21/L2 and the input capacitors define the commutation loop. Ground routing owner must return the nearby input ceramics to Q21 sources over a short broad path with stitching; avoid making the commutation return depend on distant ground copper.
Keep switch-node area small and on top; do not create a broad TEC_SW pour. Any bottom power transition requires suitably sized parallel vias, not a single signal via.
Inventory is Revision B ports.json: GND 191 pads/ports, V3V3 81, LOGIC_VIN 5, LOGIC_SW 3, LOGIC_BST 2. Supply edges span every listed port exactly within its net.

GND intentionally has no point-to-point edges. Parent MUST synthesize a continuous inner1 GND plane and verify every one of the 191 GND ports is physically connected by a legal surface escape and off-pad via or plated-hole connection. Omission is not a routed-ground claim.

Ground preferred layers are inner1, top, bottom. Do not place vias directly on fine-pitch pads; find legal escapes against actual pad polygons and all other copper, holes, and board-edge clearances before adding vias. Keep plane antipads clear of unrelated through vias.

Explicitly connect exposed pads U_MCU.pin57, U_FLASH.pin9, and U2.pin21 with short wide surface copper to multiple legal off-pad GND vias where space permits. Exposed pads must not remain isolated when fine peripheral pins are routed.

Give each decoupling capacitor ground pad a nearby individual ground via and short return to its IC ground region. Preserve continuous return under USB, QSPI, clock, ADC and control traces; add nearby GND stitching at signal layer transitions without touching signal pads.

Use multiple GND vias and wide local surface copper for Q21 source pads, U2 power grounds, TEC connector J_TEC.pin2, high-current capacitor returns and both USB connector shell/GND groups. A single thin escape is inadequate for power returns; keep switching and TEC return current local rather than through MCU/analog bypass stubs.

Join analog and digital GND to the continuous plane without splitting it. Keep high-current and buck switch loops away from thermal/ADC and crystal returns. Stitch top/bottom GND copper to inner1 at board edges and connectors only where clearance permits; suppress isolated pour islands.

V3V3 has explicit local bypass leaves and a constrained passive-endpoint minimum-distance distribution tree. IC fine-pitch pads are never transit nodes. RP2040, flash and USB-switch taps are 0.2 mm; ordinary supply taps are 0.4 mm and distribution trunks 0.6–0.8 mm. Parent must narrow local pad escapes where actual pad clearances require it.

LOGIC_BST and LOGIC_SW request top-only routing. Other V3V3 distribution prefers top, inner2, bottom to preserve inner1 as a GND return plane. Priorities place bootstrap/switch loops and local bypass taps before distribution trunks.

This is a connectivity and layer-preference plan, not a completed route or DRC result. Parent must synthesize legal geometry, ground plane/vias, verify all copper connectivity, enforce manufacturer clearances, and run shorts checks. No placement or source-net edits were made.
All selectors and pin functions are taken from ports.json and processor.tsx; no pin assignments or placements are changed.
13 complete spanning trees, 28 edges, 0.2 mm width. Crystal/QSPI priority 0; local supply priority 10; boot/reset priority 20.
Prefer top for oscillator and bypass branches. Reserve inner1 for GND; permit inner2/bottom for crossing QSPI signals and the V1V1 backbone.
Length budgets are routing targets in mm, allowing pad escape and obstacle clearance; they are not verified routed lengths or a timing/impedance signoff.
Keep oscillator copper clear of QSPI clock, USB, and switching power routes. Avoid extra oscillator vias and leave bypass return routing to the GND owner.
23 nets, 74 connected pad selectors, 51 tree edges; every endpoint is checked against ports.json.
Control traces are 0.20 mm; PD_VDD and USB_PROG_5V traces are 0.40 mm, within the corresponding pad widths.
U_INPUT signal pads are 0.25 mm tall on 0.45 mm pitch; escape outward before turns or vias. MCU control pads are nominally 0.20 mm.
Priority 5 reserves local PD sensing, decoupling, reference, and eFuse control routes. Configuration, status distribution, and USB supply taps use priority 25.
All terminals are on top. Preferred inner/bottom layers require clearance-checked top-pad escapes and vias in the route realization.
Inherited placement requires long MCU configuration/status runs and an approximately 62 mm PD_VALID_N debug branch; no connectivity or placement is changed.
Every owned net has a concrete spanning tree. All traces are 0.2 mm. Filtered sense nets have priority 2; other analog nets have priority 15.

R20.pin1 at (40.145,9.5) is the true positive shunt pickup; R20.pin2 at (45.855,9.5) is the negative pickup. The power route owner must branch R25.pin1 and R41.pin1 directly from R20.pin1, and R26.pin1 and R42.pin1 directly from R20.pin2, without using L2, capacitor or connector copper as a sense source.

Unfiltered controller Kelvin branches span approximately 29.95 mm and 30.80 mm before detours. Route them as a close pair outside the Q20/Q21/L2 switching region, then separate only at the R25/R26 filter inputs. The monitor pair spans approximately 14.62 mm and 14.65 mm and also requires independent shunt-pad pickups.

Keep filtered sense, VC, COMP_RC, RT, FB and DAC copper at least 0.5 mm from switching/gate copper where the preserved placement permits; route on a quiet alternate layer where this cannot be met on top. These are analog separation goals in addition to normal copper clearance.

C32 and C42 should connect directly to their respective input pads with short branches. The priority-2 sense routes consume the left controller escape corridor before VC and RT. Left-side U2 pads must escape left before turning; direct northbound diagonals through the row are invalid.
Length limits are routing targets for compact local links. The solver must still verify every pad escape, via, copper clearance and connection on the complete board.

C32 differential filtering is local, but the switching-node R23.pin2 at (18.65,33.45) lies near R25/R26/R28. Keep its power route outside the analog corridor and use layer separation rather than sending sense/compensation signals alongside it.
25 interlock nets use 0.2 mm signal traces and exact physical pad selectors.
Tree branch points are existing same-net pads; no electrical or placement changes.
Prefer top for local bias and pad escape, inner2 for cross-board interlock runs, bottom as the final routing alternative.
Priorities 15–30 reserve early routing for clock, clear, fault, and hardware permission paths.
No maximum signal length is imposed; the shared engine must verify clearance, connectivity, and shorts for the complete board.
Exact inventory selectors cover 36 pads using 26 edges across nine connected nets and one singleton.
POWER_BUDGET_HIGH contains only R227.pin1 in the inventory, so it intentionally has no routing edge.
All traces are 0.2 mm wide. Local divider and ADC branches prefer top; long raw and testpoint branches prefer inner2 then bottom.
Ground is owned separately. J_HOT.pin2/J_COLD.pin2, lower divider returns, and C209-C212 ground pads need local low-impedance returns to the shared reference plane.
Remote testpoints lie at x=20 to 42.75 mm, y=0.5 to 2 mm; ADC circuitry is at x=-23.58 to -13.25 mm, y=-14 to -27.7 mm. Their long branches must not displace local capacitor-to-MCU connections.
No hard maximum lengths are imposed: the inventory provides geometry but no timing, settling-time, or manufacturer limits. The common clearance-aware solver determines legal escapes and vias.
All 30 owned terminal selectors were checked against ports.json; none share a physical pad ID. Each net has exactly N-1 edges and all terminals are included.
Only the local FAN_SW and FAN_BST edges require top routing; power reservoirs use 0.8 mm, smaller power lands 0.4-0.5 mm, and controls 0.2 mm.

Current placement puts the bootstrap capacitor about 5.36 mm from U_FAN.pin6 and the feedback divider about 14.35 mm from U_FAN.pin4 before detours. Geometry must honor intervening pads; electrical loop optimization would require a separate placement change.
U_MCU pins13/14 have 0.1999996 mm pad height and 0.40005 mm pitch. Their 0.2 mm escapes must follow the horizontal pad axis; larger traces or vias placed between the pins are unsuitable.

Remote V12_FAN debug branches extend to TP04 (4,2) and R504 (-12,32.75); FAN_PWM_DRIVE and filtered tach traverse over 68 mm to the MCU. The common clearance router must add layer transitions and avoid other net copper.
Owns exactly 14 nets, 37 pads and 23 spanning-tree edges; selectors are copied from ports.json.
All traces are 0.2 mm; I2C priority is 40 and LED/debug priority is 60; layer preference is top, inner2, bottom.
SCL and SDA each use a four-edge pullup-rooted tree, keeping the MCU pad a leaf and the nearby testpoint stub short.
The eight resistor-to-LED anode links stay local on top; do not change LED or resistor placements.
Use the parent clearance-aware solver for pad escapes, layer transitions and final copper geometry; these trees add no component moves or connectivity changes.
